author: Jason Stys
summary: Install bounded, credential-aware Node-RED metadata nodes. Final TGZ tests now use a real separate Node-RED runtime and HTTP provider to verify success, routing, retry, cooldown and cancellation; compatible tooling fixes and full-graph auditing address the exposed dependency findings.
rationale: Tests the distributed package at its actual message and network boundary and closes the security gap left by a partial dependency audit.
limitations: Synthetic local providers and in-memory fixture storage exercise the installed node lifecycle, not a production editor deployment, external provider availability or persistent flow configuration.
The Node-RED host remains a separate installation responsibility. No new public npm publication or native desktop installer is supplied.
Known-advisory audit results are time-specific and do not prove absence of vulnerabilities; checksum evidence does not establish publisher authentication.

visualReview.method: Every rendered page individually viewed at readable original resolution

scope: Reviewed documentation editions of the cited source. Checksums identify bytes, not authorship. Historical measurements retain their own dates; integration CI must be checked separately.
